paper.title: November 2024 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL Paper 1 TZ2
paper.solution_status: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider the following set of ordered data.

22, 22, 26, 27, 28, 32, 36, 38, 39, 42

(a) Write down
    (i) the mode;
    (ii) the range;
    (iii) the median. [3]

(b) Find the interquartile range. [3]
questions.summary: Calculate central tendency and spread for ordered data.
questions.solution: (a)(i) Mode = 22. (ii) Range = 20. (iii) Median = 30. (b) Q₁ = 26, Q₃ = 38, hence IQR = 38 − 26 = 12.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Points A and B lie on a circle with centre O and radius r cm, where AÔB = 1.5 radians.

[Diagram not to scale: sector OAB, with radii OA and OB and central angle AÔB labelled 1.5.]

The area of sector OAB is 48 cm².

(a) Find r. [3]

(b) Hence, find the perimeter of sector OAB. [2]
questions.summary: Use sector area and arc length.
questions.solution: (a) ½r²θ=48, so ½r²(1.5)=48; therefore r=8 cm. (b) Perimeter = 2r+rθ = 28 cm.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

Two events A and B satisfy P(A) = 0.65, P(B) = 0.45 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.85.

(a) Find P(A ∩ B). [3]

(b) Find P(A′ | B′). [3]

4. [Maximum mark: 4]

Prove that (3n + 2)² − (3n − 2)² is a multiple of 12 for all n ∈ ℤ⁺.
questions.summary: Prove divisibility by a difference of squares.
questions.solution: Using a²−b²=(a+b)(a−b), (3n + 2)²−(3n − 2)² = 24n = 12(2n). Since the remaining factor is integral for n∈ℤ⁺, it is a multiple of 12.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Triangle ABC has AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm, AC = 5 cm and AB̂C = 2θ.

[Diagram not to scale: triangle ABC with the three sides labelled as stated and angle at B labelled 2θ.]

Find the exact value of cos θ, giving your answer in the form (p√2)/q, where p, q ∈ ℤ⁺.
questions.summary: Use cosine rule and a half-angle identity.
questions.solution: Cosine rule gives cos(2θ)=(4²+6²−5²)/(2·4·6). Then cos²θ=(1+cos2θ)/2. Taking the positive root gives cosθ=5√2/8.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

For an arithmetic sequence, u₁₀ = 16 and S₂₅ = 100.

Find k such that uₖ = 0.
questions.summary: Solve an arithmetic sequence from a term and sum.
questions.solution: Let first term be a and difference d. Then a+9d=16 and 25/2(2a+24d)=100. Solving gives d=−4, a=52. Setting a+(k−1)d=0 gives k=14.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 16]

Graphs of f and g are shown. f is linear with x-intercept (4, 0) and y-intercept (0, 8). g has x-intercepts (−2, 0), (4, 0) and y-intercept (0, 8).

[Diagram: a descending line through (0, 8) and (4, 0), and a downward parabola through all three stated intercepts; the parabola is above the line between x=0 and x=4.]

(a) Write f(x)=mx+c. [2]

g(x)=−x²+bx+8.

(b) Find b. [3]

(c) Show that the enclosed area is ∫₀⁴(−x² + 4x) dx. [2]

(d) Hence find the area. [4]

At P on g, the tangent is parallel to f.

(e) Find P. [5]
questions.summary: Find equations, enclosed area, and a parallel tangent.
questions.solution: (a) Slope=−2, so f(x)=−2x + 8. (b) Substitution of (4,0) gives b=2. (c) g−f=−x² + 4x, so area=∫₀⁴(−x² + 4x) dx. (d) Integrating gives 32/3 square units. (e) g′(x)=−2x+2; equate to −2 and substitute in g, giving P=(2, 8).

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 14]

f(x)=log₂(4x), x>0.

(a) Find (i) f(8); (ii) f(1/4). [3]

(b) Find f⁻¹(x). [4]

(c) Hence, or otherwise, find f⁻¹(0). [1]

The graph y=f(16x³) is obtained by translating and stretching y=log₂x.

(d) Describe the two transformations, including their order. [6]
questions.summary: Evaluate and invert logarithms and describe transformations.
questions.solution: (a)(i) f(8)=5; (ii) f(1/4)=0. (b) From y=log₂(4x), 2ʸ=4x, so f⁻¹(x)=2ˣ/4. (c) f⁻¹(0)=1/4. (d) f(16x³)=log₂(64x³)=6+3log₂x. First stretch vertically by factor 3, then translate 6 units upward.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 17]

A cylinder has radius 4r and height h. A central cylinder of radius r is removed.

[Diagram: vertical hollow cylinder of height h; hole radius r and radial wall thickness 3r.]

Surface area is S and volume is V.

(a) Show S=30πr²+10πrh. [3]

(b) Given S=240π cm², show V=360πr−45πr³. [6]

(c) Find dV/dr. [2]

Maximum volume occurs when r=p√(2/3), p∈ℤ⁺.

(d) Find p. [3]

(e) Hence find the maximum volume in the form qπ√(2/3), q∈ℤ⁺. [3]
questions.summary: Model and optimize a hollow cylinder.
questions.solution: (a) Two annuli give 30πr²; curved surfaces give 10πrh. (b) S=240π gives rh=24−3r². Thus V=15πr²h=15πr(24−3r²)=360πr−45πr³. (c) dV/dr=360π−135πr². (d) Set derivative zero: r²=8/3, so r=2√(2/3), p=2; d²V/dr²<0. (e) Substitution gives Vmax=480π√(2/3) cm³, q=480.
